dish: the classic French tasting menu (the legendary Bresse-pigeon and truffle courses)
w: A three-MICHELIN-star destination hidden in a village near Wittlich on the edge of the Mosel/Eifel, long the life's work of Helmut Thieltges and now carried on at the top by Clemens Rambichler. Uncompromising, produce-driven classic French cuisine ranked among Germany's very best tables — a pilgrimage worth the detour off the river.

dish: fresh Mosel trout (Forelle) prepared to a fourth-generation recipe
w: Set in what is said to be Germany's oldest wine-tavern building, in a family's hands for some 350 years. The kitchen sends out seasonal gourmet menus and a daily-changing 'fairy-tale menu', but the signature is river trout to a recipe handed down four generations — the definitive traditional table in Bernkastel-Kues.

dish: Mosel-Maultaschen and house wine aspic (Weinsülze) with estate Riesling
w: A down-to-earth wine restaurant in the old town with one of Trier's loveliest terraces, pouring the wines of the Bischöfliche Weingüter, the Friedrich-Wilhelm-Gymnasium estate and Weingut Rinke by the glass. Regional cooking — Mosel-Maultaschen, homemade Weinsülze, calf's liver with apple — with a light Levantine touch from the Beirut-born chef.

dish: vintner's plate (Winzerteller) with estate Mosel Riesling in the Weinstube
w: A family estate in Trier's Olewig wine district (about 3 km from the centre), listed by the Deutsches Weininstitut, known for high-quality Riesling and Burgundy wines. Its cosy Weinstube pairs those wines with classic vintner's cooking — the authentic way to taste Trier as a wine town.

dish: Olewig Riesling, Weißburgunder and Auxerrois at a vineyard-side tasting
w: A working family winery in Trier-Olewig with the vineyard directly behind the house, offering tastings of Riesling, Weißer Burgunder, Auxerrois, Gewürztraminer and Sauvignon Blanc. A relaxed, authentic stop for Trier's own steep-slope wines.

dish: handmade Torten, croissants and cakes from the in-house Konditorei (since 1953)
w: A traditional Trier café-confectionery founded in 1953 on a quiet lane minutes from the Dom and Hauptmarkt, everything baked daily in-house from largely regional ingredients. Elegantly renovated in 2018, it is the classic address for Kaffee und Kuchen in the old town.

dish: 150+ Mosel, Saar and Ruwer Rieslings poured by the glass
w: In the vaulted cellars of the medieval Cusanusstift, the largest Riesling vinotheque on the Mosel — more than 150 wines from Mosel, Saar and Ruwer available by the glass, chosen each year by a jury. Rick Steves names it the place to start tasting Mosel wine; the single best one-stop introduction to the region's Riesling.

dish: Riesling tasting with fresh Flammkuchen at the Rieslingmanufaktur
w: Johannes and Doris Schmitz's 'Rieslingmanufaktur' in the wine village of Ürzig, below the famous Würzgarten slope. Tastings run from classic flights to culinary themes, with fresh Flammkuchen a favourite accompaniment — a warm, personal way to drink steep-slate Mosel Riesling at source.

dish: Piesporter Goldtröpfchen Riesling at the estate
w: One of Piesport's historic family estates in the heart of the Middle Mosel, with holdings in the celebrated Piesporter Goldtröpfchen. 'Quality on our mind, Riesling in our heart' — a well-regarded address (listed by wein.plus) to taste one of the Mosel's most famous single vineyards.

dish: Mosel-Franconian Pfännchen and grilled steaks with local wine
w: A family-run restaurant-cum-wine-tavern in a former butcher's shop, its walls crammed with antique wine tools and a little museum's worth of Mosel memorabilia. Hearty, seasonal Mosel-Franconian cooking — Pfännchen, grilled steaks, small plates to drink wine with — a beloved Traben-Trarbach institution since 1970.

dish: regional Mosel cooking with estate wine in a 14th-century inn
w: Set in the Alte Thorschenke, one of Germany's oldest inns (1332) at Cochem's old town gate, all beams, winding stairs and history. Regional Mosel dishes and estate wines served in the panelled rooms or on the terrace — atmospheric traditional dining in the shadow of the Reichsburg.

dish: Zeller Schwarze Katz Riesling flights from the town's growers
w: Zell's town vinotheque on the Mosel promenade, dedicated to the 'Zeller Schwarze Katz' — the legendary Black-Cat Riesling — with wines from the local growers to taste and buy. The place to try the wine behind the famous label at its home.

dish: regional Saar cooking with the estate's own Saar Riesling (30+ by the glass)
w: A Weinstube in the old town of Saarburg pouring 30-plus open wines and sekt from the family's own Saar vineyards alongside regional cooking. On the Saar edge of the Mosel wine country, where the cuisine takes as much from nearby France as from Germany.
